subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Should OpenClaw solve this with the broader `tools.fs.roots` host-filesystem policy, a narrower media-only local-root config, or no new configurable host-root surface?
rationale: The implementation changes which host paths model-facing media tools can read, and repository policy treats new config plus filesystem/media-root access as a security and compatibility boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Adopt central fs roots
options.body: Use a single reviewed `tools.fs.roots`-style policy for read/media surfaces so OpenClaw does not grow competing allowlists.

options.title: Design media-only roots
options.body: Add a narrower media-root field only after documenting why it should differ from filesystem-tool roots and channel inbound roots.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Decline configurable host roots and require copying, symlinking, or channel-scoped inbound-root handling instead.

recommendation.title: Adopt central fs roots
recommendation.body: Use a single reviewed `tools.fs.roots`-style policy for read/media surfaces so OpenClaw does not grow competing allowlists.

likelyOwner.reason: Jacob recently owned the merged local-root policy change that intentionally kept root expansion configuration-derived.
